title: stage masks: spotlight
shortDescription: Ward C, 3:07 a.m.: a flooded asylum corridor seen only through a fog of war, the slot of a StageDirector masked by a living mask stage
description:
A `StageDirector` with three slots: the deep black water at the bottom, the level in the middle, the player on top. The level's slot is masked: `director.setMask(level, new StageMask(fog))`. The mask stage `fog` is a `Stage2D` of soft blobs over transparent black — a pool around the player, a beam ahead of the torch and three sodium lamps that hum, swing and die — and the level shows only where they are. Below it the deep shows through, and something watches from the very rim of the light.

The mask belongs to the **slot**, not to the level: *next level* calls `replace(level, nextLevel)` with a crossfade, and an all-night laundromat fades in behind the same porthole; `maskOf()` of the new level answers the same mask. *source* picks what of the mask picture is the coverage — the lamps are sodium orange and the torch a cold white, so `blue` leaves only the torch and `red` both; *invert* turns the porthole inside out. Both are read when a `StageMask` is made, so a switch makes a new mask and sets it on the slot. *mask on the slot* is `setMask(level, undefined)` and back. Walk with WASD, the arrow keys or a pointer drag. See [Stage masks: a fog of war over a level](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#a-fog-of-war-over-a-level) and [masks on a slot](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#masks-on-a-slot).
